title: Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) | NHS inform
text:
Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis)
Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) is common. It can develop at any age but often starts in childhood or puberty.
Symptoms of excessive sweating
Excessive sweating can cause visible sweat, wet clothes and clammy palms. It may affect the whole body or only certain areas like the hands and feet. Both sides of the body are usually affected equally. For example, both feet or both hands.
What you can do to help excessive sweating
There are some things you can do yourself to help excessive sweating.
Do
wear loose, light clothing
wear socks that absorb moisture – like sports socks
change your socks at least twice a day
try to wear shoes made of leather
alternate your shoes each day
Don’t
do not have things that can make excessive sweating worse
–
like alcohol and spicy food
do not wear clothes made from man-made fibres like nylon
do not wear tight, restrictive clothing
Treatment for excessive sweating
You can buy some treatments for excessive sweating yourself without a prescription. This includes:
strong antiperspirants
armpit or sweat shields to absorb excessive sweat and protect your clothing
foot powders for sweaty feet
soap substitutes that are more gentle on your skin
Other treatments for excessive sweating
It may take time to find the right treatment for excessive sweating.
Excessive sweating can sometimes be cause by another condition. This means the best treatment for you will depend on what the cause is.
Your GP may refer you to a specialist in treating skin conditions (dermatologist) if:
there’s no obvious cause for your excessive sweating
nothing seems to be helping
A dermatologist may suggest other treatments you can try like:
medicines that reduce sweating
iontophoresis
–
a weak electric current is passed through water or a wet pad to the affected area
Botox injections in the affected area (this may not be available on the NHS)
surgery – for example, removal of the sweat glands
Speak to your GP practice if:
You’re sweating excessively and:
things you can do yourself are not helping
it’s lasted at least 6 months
it stops you from getting on with your daily activities
it happens at least once a week
it happens at night (night sweats)
you have a family history of excessive sweating
you’re taking medicine for another condition
The GP may refer you for tests if they think another condition may be causing your sweating.
What causes excessive sweating?
It’s normal to sweat when you’re hot or when you’re doing physical activity. However, if you’re sweating a lot when your body doesn’t need to cool down, this is excessive sweating.
Often there’s no obvious cause for excessive sweating. This is known as primary hyperhidrosis.
Secondary hyperhidrosis is when a cause for excessive sweating can be found. Some reasons for excessive sweating include:
certain medications
menopause
pregnancy
obesity
hormonal conditions like an
overactive thyroid
diabetes
infection
low blood sugar (
hypoglycaemia
)
Secondary hyperhidrosis often starts more suddenly than primary hyperhidrosis. It usually affects the whole body.
Complications of excessive sweating
Excessive sweating isn’t usually serious, but it can increase the risk of fungal infections. For example, athlete’s foot or
fungal nail infections.
This is because excessive sweat, along with wearing socks and shoes, help fungi to grow.
Excessive sweating can also make you more vulnerable to skin conditions like
warts
.
Some activities may be harder if your hands are affected by excessive sweating. For example, writing, using a keyboard, playing some sports or playing an instrument.
Excessive sweating doesn’t usually affect the sweat glands that produce unpleasant-smelling sweat. This means excessive sweating doesn’t cause a bad smell. However, a harmless skin bacteria can build up if you sweat excessively which can cause an unpleasant smell.
Living with excessive sweating
Excessive sweating can make you feel self-conscious and anxious. This may be worse in certain situations, like meeting new people or being in a crowded room. These feelings can also make excessive sweating worse, creating a cycle.
A self-help guide may give you tips on how to manage anxiety.
